extracted.intended_audience: devout Christian readers seeking guidance in the interior/spiritual life; translators and editors of L'Imitation de Jésus‑Christ
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and ascetic precepts for entering the interior life and imitating Jesus Christ (chapter‑by‑chapter maxims and reflections), plus editorial/translation guidance about rendering the work in French. Intended as actionable guidance for living and for preparing editions/translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qu'il faut imiter JÉSUS-CHRIST, et mépriser toutes les vanités du monde
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter I: 'Qu'il faut imiter JÉSUS-CHRIST, et mépriser toutes les vanités du monde.' The principal study should be to meditate on the life of Jesus Christ; all worldly riches, honors, bodily desires and temporal attachments are vanity compared with loving and serving God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meditate on and conform your life to Jesus Christ rather than intellectualizing scripture; detach heart from visible things and accumulate an imperishable treasure (Matth., VI, 20). Anti-patterns: seeking riches, honors, sensual satisfaction, or long life without concern for living well; treating religion as mere intellectual admiration without humility and transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoir d'humbles sentiments de soi-même (humility over knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter II: 'Avoir d'humbles sentiments de soi-même.' Humility of heart is superior to mere knowledge: science without fear of God is of little value; the truly wise love to live unknown and be accounted as nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderate the desire to know; avoid pride in learning. Prefer a holy life and pure conscience over intellectual display. Anti-patterns: seeking reputation for learning, allowing knowledge to inflate judgment, neglecting practice for theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: De la Doctrine de vérité (seek truth, not verbal subtlety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter III: 'De la Doctrine de vérité.' Seek the truth itself rather than empty subtleties, figures or disputations; prefer the living Word (Verbe) speaking within and direct assimilation of truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid being consumed by speculative disputes or genre/term debates that do not serve salvation; cultivate interior recollection to receive divine light. Anti-patterns: valuing academic argument over sanctity; being distracted by classifications while ignoring duty to live rightly.

rubrics_metrics.name: De la Prévoyance dans les actions (prudence and counsel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter IV: 'De la Prévoyance dans les actions.' Do not accept every word or interior movement; weigh things according to God, avoid precipitate action, and seek the advice of the wise and consciencious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice careful deliberation and humility when making important decisions; consult someone wiser and more devout rather than acting on pride or impulse. Anti-patterns: acting precipitately, trusting one’s own understanding without counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: De la lecture de l'Écriture sainte (read Scripture for truth, not eloquence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter V: 'De la lecture de l'Écriture sainte.' Read Sacred Scripture to seek truth and usefulness, not rhetorical elegance; read with humility, simplicity and faith and avoid intellectual curiosity that hinders fruit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach Scripture in the spirit it was given; value simple, pious books as well as deep ones; do not read to appear learned. Anti-patterns: treating Scripture as a text for display or debate rather than for forming faith and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Des Affections déréglées (resist disordered passions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter VI: 'Des Affections déréglées.' When desires become disordered the soul is troubled; true peace comes by resisting passions rather than satisfying them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate mortification of concupiscence and patience under temptation; understand that succumbing brings remorse and loss of peace. Anti-patterns: yielding to appetites expecting peace; confusing gratification with true serenity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qu'il faut fuir l'orgueil et les vaines espérances (flee pride and false hopes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter VII: 'Qu'il faut fuir l'orgueil et les vaines espérances.' Do not place hope in men or creatures; trust only in God; do not glory in riches, friends, bodily strength, or even your good works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice low estimate of self and esteem of others to preserve humility; avoid complacency about apparent virtues. Anti-patterns: boasting of works, trusting in social standing, presumption about one’s perseverance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Éviter la trop grande familiarité (avoid excessive familiarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter VIII: 'Éviter la trop grande familiarité.' Do not open your heart indiscriminately; confide in the wise and God alone; limit social intercourse (especially with worldly youth and the powerful) and prefer the humble and pious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep conversation edifying; avoid excessive intimacy that divides and weakens the soul; prefer the company of those of good morals. Anti-patterns: flattering the rich, seeking wide social familiarity, exposing one’s heart to unsuited company.

rubrics_metrics.name: De l'obéissance et du renoncement à son propre sens (obedience and renunciation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter IX (heading): 'De l'obéissance et du renoncement à son propre sens.' Living under a superior in obedience and renouncing one’s own will is presented as a high spiritual good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer obedience to commanding; submit willingly rather than murmuring; avoid dependence on one’s own judgment. (Text truncated, but surrounding chapters emphasize humility, counsel, and renunciation as recurring norms.) Anti-patterns: valuing independence, resisting legitimate authority out of pride.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edition practice: place 'Réflexions' at end of chapters to aid practice
rubrics_metrics.description: From the Preface / P.S.: Place short 'Réflexions' (reflections/practices) at the end of each chapter to serve as summaries and practical exercises, modeled on the practices of P. Gonnelieu but adapted for times lacking simple faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise practical points at chapter ends to fix attention on main precepts; use them as an aid for practice rather than purely historical or devotional ornament. Anti-patterns: inserting outdated or irrelevant 'practices' without adaptation; presenting reflections as mere commentary rather than practical steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and editorial criteria for L'Imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Preface discussion of translations: evaluate translations by fidelity to the original, warmth/unction ('onction'), precision, and capacity to reproduce the original’s animated, picturesque expression rather than mere elegant paraphrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer translations that (a) faithfully render the original text, (b) preserve its spiritual warmth and expressive force, and (c) avoid slavish copying of previous translators or mere paraphrase that loses onction. Examples/antipatterns in Preface: Marillac praised for closeness to original and naïveté; Saci criticized as elegant paraphrase; Beauzée 'correct' but lacking warmth; P. Lallemant precise but dry; the celebrated 'P. Gonnelieu' edition is actually a printer's assemblage and often inferior. Editors/translators should combine the good of older translations while seeking fidelity to the beauties of the original.
